issues.detail: The Greek 'ομοιωθησεται' (homoiōthēsetai) is a passive verb meaning 'will be likened to' or 'will be compared to'. The Vietnamese translation 'sẽ giống như' (will be like) treats the comparison as an identity or a direct simile without capturing the passive/comparative nature of the Greek construction.

The Greek phrase 'αιτινες λαβουσαι τας λαμπαδας αυτων' (who, having taken their lamps) is simplified in Vietnamese to 'cầm đèn của mình'. While the meaning is largely preserved, the causal/participial nuance of 'having taken' is lost.
